topics.title: What is Bitcoin?
points: Digital currency with no central authority
Runs on a public ledger called blockchain
Capped supply of 21 million coins ever

topics.title: What is Blockchain?
points: A chain of blocks storing transaction records
Distributed across thousands of computers
Once written, data can't be altered

topics.title: Hot Wallet vs Cold Wallet
points: Hot wallets stay online, convenient for spending
Cold wallets stay offline, safer for savings
Never share your seed phrase with anyone

topics.title: What is a Private Key?
points: Your private key proves ownership of funds
Whoever has the key controls the coins
Lose it and your funds are gone forever

topics.title: How Does Crypto Mining Work?
points: Miners solve puzzles to validate transactions
Winner adds the next block and earns rewards
Requires serious computing power and electricity

topics.title: What is Bitcoin Halving?
points: Mining rewards cut in half every 4 years
Less new BTC entering circulation over time
Historically precedes major bull market cycles

topics.title: Market Cap Explained
points: Price multiplied by circulating supply
Shows a coin's total market value
Higher cap usually means lower volatility

topics.title: What is an Altcoin?
points: Any cryptocurrency that isn't Bitcoin
Thousands exist, each with different goals
Higher risk, but sometimes higher reward

topics.title: What is a Stablecoin?
points: Pegged to a stable asset like the US dollar
Used to avoid crypto's price swings
Popular examples: USDT, USDC, DAI

topics.title: What Are Gas Fees?
points: Fee paid to process a blockchain transaction
Goes to miners or validators, not the platform
Rises when the network is congested

topics.title: What Does HODL Mean?
points: Originated from a typo of 'hold' in 2013
Now means holding through market volatility
A long-term investing mindset, not a strategy

topics.title: FOMO vs FUD
points: FOMO: Fear Of Missing Out on gains
FUD: Fear, Uncertainty, Doubt spread to scare sellers
Both drive irrational, emotional trading decisions

topics.title: ATH and ATL Explained
points: ATH = All-Time High, the highest price ever
ATL = All-Time Low, the lowest price ever
Traders watch both as key psychological levels

topics.title: Support and Resistance
points: Support: a price floor buyers defend
Resistance: a price ceiling sellers defend
Breaking either level often signals a new trend

topics.title: Market Order vs Limit Order
points: Market order: buy/sell instantly at current price
Limit order: set your own target price
Limit orders offer control, market orders offer speed

topics.title: What is Liquidity?
points: How easily an asset converts to cash
High liquidity means tighter, fairer prices
Low liquidity means bigger price swings on trades

topics.title: Understanding Volatility
points: How much and how fast prices move
Crypto is far more volatile than stocks
Higher volatility means higher risk and reward

topics.title: What is Slippage?
points: Difference between expected and actual trade price
Happens most in low-liquidity markets
Bigger orders cause more slippage

topics.title: Leverage Trading Basics
points: Borrowing funds to open a bigger position
Amplifies both profits and losses equally
High leverage can wipe out your account fast

topics.title: What is Short Selling?
points: Betting that an asset's price will fall
Borrow, sell high, buy back low, return it
Profit is the difference, but losses are uncapped

topics.title: What is DeFi?
points: Decentralized Finance: banking without banks
Lending, borrowing, and trading via smart contracts
Open to anyone with an internet connection

topics.title: What is Yield Farming?
points: Lending or staking crypto to earn rewards
Returns come from fees or new tokens
Higher yields usually mean higher risk

topics.title: Liquidity Pools Explained
points: Pooled funds that power decentralized exchanges
Users deposit pairs of tokens to earn fees
Prices are set by the pool's own formula

topics.title: What is Staking?
points: Locking up coins to help secure the network
Earn rewards for validating transactions
Alternative to energy-heavy mining

topics.title: Impermanent Loss Explained
points: Loss from providing liquidity vs just holding
Happens when paired token prices diverge
Fees earned can offset but not always cover it

topics.title: DEX vs CEX
points: DEX: trade directly from your wallet, no signup
CEX: centralized exchange, holds funds for you
DEX offers control, CEX offers convenience

topics.title: What is a Smart Contract?
points: Self-executing code that runs on the blockchain
Automatically enforces the terms of an agreement
Powers most of DeFi and NFTs

topics.title: How Crypto Lending Works
points: Deposit crypto, earn interest from borrowers
Borrowers post collateral to secure the loan
Rates float based on supply and demand

topics.title: What is a Flash Loan?
points: Borrow with no collateral, repay in one transaction
Entire loan reverses if not repaid instantly
Used for arbitrage, but also exploited by hackers

topics.title: What is TVL?
points: Total Value Locked: funds deposited in a protocol
Key metric for judging DeFi platform size
Rising TVL often signals growing trust

topics.title: Consensus Mechanisms Explained
points: Rules that get network participants to agree
Prevents fraud without a central authority
Proof of Work and Proof of Stake are most common

topics.title: Proof of Work vs Proof of Stake
points: PoW: miners compete using computing power
PoS: validators are chosen based on stake
PoS uses far less energy than PoW

topics.title: Layer 1 vs Layer 2
points: Layer 1: the base blockchain, like Ethereum
Layer 2: built on top to boost speed
L2s reduce fees while inheriting L1 security

topics.title: What is Sharding?
points: Splits the network into smaller pieces
Each shard processes transactions in parallel
Massively increases blockchain throughput

topics.title: What is a Node?
points: A computer that stores a copy of the blockchain
Validates and relays transactions across the network
More nodes mean a more decentralized system

topics.title: Hard Fork vs Soft Fork
points: Hard fork: a permanent split, creates a new chain
Soft fork: backward-compatible rule update
Forks often happen over protocol disagreements

topics.title: What is Interoperability?
points: Different blockchains communicating with each other
Lets assets move across separate networks
Bridges are the most common solution today

topics.title: What is an Oracle?
points: Feeds real-world data into smart contracts
Blockchains can't access outside data on their own
Critical for price feeds and DeFi accuracy

topics.title: Why Gas Fees Spike
points: Network congestion drives fees higher
Everyone bids for limited block space
Layer 2s exist specifically to solve this

topics.title: What is a Rollup?
points: Bundles many transactions into one L1 transaction
Cuts fees dramatically while keeping security
Two types: optimistic and zero-knowledge

topics.title: What is an NFT?
points: A unique, non-interchangeable digital token
Proves ownership of art, items, or access
Lives on the blockchain, unlike a regular file

topics.title: ERC-20 vs ERC-721
points: ERC-20: standard for interchangeable tokens
ERC-721: standard for unique, one-of-a-kind NFTs
Both run on Ethereum's shared infrastructure

topics.title: What is Tokenomics?
points: The economic design behind a crypto token
Covers supply, distribution, and incentives
Bad tokenomics can doom even a good project

topics.title: What is a Token Burn?
points: Permanently removes tokens from circulation
Reduces total supply to support scarcity
Often used to try to boost token value

topics.title: What is an Airdrop?
points: Free tokens sent to eligible wallet holders
Often rewards early users of a protocol
Used to build community and spread ownership

topics.title: What is Vesting?
points: Tokens released gradually over time
Prevents early investors from dumping instantly
Protects price stability after a launch

topics.title: Utility Tokens vs Governance Tokens
points: Utility: used to access a product or service
Governance: used to vote on protocol decisions
Some tokens serve both purposes at once

topics.title: What is a DAO?
points: Decentralized Autonomous Organization, run by code
Members vote using governance tokens
No CEO — decisions are made collectively

topics.title: How to Read a Whitepaper
points: Explains a project's tech, goals, and tokenomics
Check the team, roadmap, and real use case
A vague whitepaper is often a red flag

topics.title: What is a Token Unlock?
points: Scheduled release of previously locked tokens
Can increase circulating supply significantly
Large unlocks often pressure price downward

topics.title: Seed Phrase Safety
points: 12-24 words that restore your entire wallet
Never type it into a website or share it
Store it offline, on paper or metal

topics.title: How to Spot a Rug Pull
points: Devs abandon a project and drain funds
Watch for anonymous teams and locked liquidity
Be wary of promises of guaranteed returns

topics.title: Common Crypto Phishing Scams
points: Fake wallet pop-ups asking you to 'verify'
Impersonators posing as support in DMs
Always double check URLs before connecting a wallet

topics.title: Why You Need 2FA
points: Adds a second layer beyond your password
Blocks most account takeover attempts
Use an authenticator app, not SMS, when possible

topics.title: What is Cold Storage?
points: Keeping private keys completely offline
Immune to online hacking attempts
Best practice for long-term holdings

topics.title: Why Smart Contract Audits Matter
points: Independent review of a contract's code
Catches bugs before hackers can exploit them
No audit is a major red flag for any protocol

topics.title: Crypto Regulation Basics
points: Rules vary hugely from country to country
Covers exchanges, taxes, and token classification
Regulatory news often moves markets fast

topics.title: What is a CBDC?
points: Central Bank Digital Currency, issued by governments
Different from crypto — fully centralized and controlled
Many countries are piloting their own versions

topics.title: Crypto Taxes 101
points: Most countries tax crypto as property or income
Selling, swapping, and spending can all be taxable
Keep records of every trade you make

topics.title: Why Diversification Matters
points: Spreading risk across multiple assets
Reduces impact of any single coin crashing
Doesn't guarantee profit, but limits damage
